chunks: Hakim ibn Dawud ibn Hakim narrated to me, he said: Salamah narrated to me, he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Mu'mmar ibn Khallad from Abul Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
As al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was traveling in the depth of the night, while he was heading to Iraq, a man was reciting poetry and saying:

O my camel! Do not be frightened by my scolding, and prepare yourself before the rising of dawn with the best of riders and the best of journeys, until you adorn yourself with the noble of status, the generous of lineage, the broad of chest. May Allah reveal him for the best of affairs, and keep him there for the duration of time.

So al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: I shall proceed, and death is not a disgrace upon the young man if he intends truth and strives as a Muslim, and supports the righteous men with his self, and leaves the ruined one and opposes the criminal. If I live, I shall not be hasty (or regret), and if I die, I shall not be blamed. Humiliation is sufficient for you if you live and are trampled.

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Mu'mmar ibn Khallad from al-Rida (peace be upon him), similar to the words of Salamah.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the Pleased One), a title for Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.مَثْبُوراً: The ruined one (one who has lost his way or faith)
key_terms.يَرْتَجِزُ: Reciting poetry in the meter of rajaz

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Husayn say about death and honor during his journey to Iraq?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the spiritual fortitude of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) during his journey to Karbala, where he encounters a jinn or man reciting poetry that affirms his noble lineage and destined martyrdom. The Imam’s response underscores the Shia theological principle that death in the path of truth is a source of honor, contrasting it with the disgrace of enduring humiliation while alive. This poetic exchange serves as a foundational text for understanding the emotional and spiritual dimensions of the Ahl al-Bayt's sacrifice.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain, from Mu’ammar ibn Khallād, who said: Abul Ḥasan (Imam Riďā (a.s.)) said:
As Ḥusain (a.s.) was traveling toward Iraq, he heard a man recite this poem in the middle of the night:

O my camel! Do not be frightened by my scolding and break out before the rising of dawn. (Carry me to) the best of riders on the best of journeys until you arrive at the most honourable place. (Carry me to Ḥusain (a.s.)) whose grandfather is the most glorious grandfather and Ḥusain (a.s.) is the most magnanimous one. Verily Allāh has chosen him for the best of affairs. May he remain until the end of time!

So Ḥusain (a.s.) replied by reciting the following poem: I shall go toward death and there is no shame for a man in death as long as his intentions are based on the truth and he fights (for Allāh) as a Muslim. (There is no shame in death for men) as long as they support the righteous ones, fight the criminals, and abandon the sinners. (I shall fight) and if I live, I shall not have any regrets. And if I am killed, I will not be blamed. Nothing is more humiliating than living under the humiliation of the oppressors.
The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Mu’ammar ibn Khallād, from Imam Riďā (a.s.).
